column1: # Unit remaining batch: owner <TAB> M <TAB> old <TAB> descriptor <TAB> semantic name
# Setters pair with the already-renamed getters through the field they assign, so those names are
# mechanical (a(int)->this.a getId -> setId, b(int)->this.m getCount -> setCount, and so on).
# The behavioural ones are backed by their bodies:
#   h(Unit) canCaptureUnit  = other owner differs && b.canCapture() && other.isCapturable()
#     This is the strongest kind of evidence: it independently confirms the UnitType batch names
#     canCapture (field x) and isCapturable (field y), themselves derived from the matrix and the
#   i(Unit) canAttackUnit   = enemy team, alive, visible via player.getFogOfWar().isUnitVisible,
#     not garrisoned and b.getDamageAgainst(other.getUnitType()) > 0 - confirms that getDamageAgainst
#     returns OUTGOING damage, exactly as the UnitType batch concluded from the AttackNearestNode /
#   g(Unit) canGuard   = same owner, same domain, neither flying, target mobile.
#   f(Unit) canProduceOrCarry = carries it already, or same owner and b.getCanProduce() has its type.
#   e(Unit) canEmbark  = f(unit) && subUnits.size() < b.getCapacity()  (so f() is the precondition).
#   d(Unit) canInteractWith = other.canEmbark(this) || canGuard || canCaptureUnit || canAttackUnit.
#   r()/s()/t() ask the same three questions about the CURRENT guard target (this.f): friendly,
#     attackable, capturable. WorldSimulator:334 uses s() and t() exactly that way.
#   f() isHighValue = b.A() (the General-only UnitType flag) or any carried unit is high value;
#     InitAttackPlan:56 gives such units a target-priority bonus.
#   j(Unit) fireAt = builds the AmmoType/target/trajectory in the Volley (this.A) and sets B = true.
#   T()/d(float) are field C: WorldSimulator:703 compares T() against the sim clock and line 725
#     stores now + reload there, so it is the time the unit may act again.
#   D()/d(int) are field p: decremented per salvo (WorldSimulator:727) and tested as <= 0 when
#     hasSalvo() is set, so it is the remaining salvo count.
# 27 rows stay blank. They fall into three groups, none of which can be named from evidence:
#   (1) trivial @Override stubs returning false (a(), b()) and methods whose field has no
#       established meaning anywhere yet (v()/b(float) field l, E/e(int) field q, F/f(int) field r,
#       H/a(boolean) field t, L/g(int) field w, B(), k(Unit));
#   (2) methods with NO evidence at all: several are private and were never read.
#   (3) NINE 2-letter accessors (Y, Z, aa, ad, ae, af, ag, ai, ak) whose bodies are IDENTICAL to
#       getMoveTargetPosition, getGuardFollowers, isVolleyActive, isEffectActive). They are almost
#       certainly implementations of OTHER interfaces methods, so renaming them to the same names
#       would both collide and mislabel them - the correct name must come from the interface side.
#       The tool would drop them on collision anyway.
# Also deliberately blank: the private duplicate setters c(UnitList) and d(UnitList), which assign
# the same fields as a(UnitList)/b(UnitList); naming both pairs identically would collide.
